abstract: Synthetic biology can program cellular behavior but remains underused in regenerative medicine. This commentary argues that integrating synthetic biology with tissue engineering should target vascularization and immune integration through compact, context-aware circuits. Embedded within engineered tissues, these circuits could enable adaptive grafts that sense stress and coordinate regenerative responses.
